quotes.text: In this challenge, participants will build an interactive application that leverages radar remote sensing data from NISAR to track and visualize one or more types of surface changes, at locations around the world. Participants are encouraged to design intuitive tools and innovative visualizations, such as interactive change-detection maps, time-series animations, or dashboards, that make NISAR data accessible to a broad audience. The desired outcome is an open-source, user-friendly solution that translates complex radar observations into actionable insights, helping scientists, resource managers, educators, decision-makers, and the public better understand the patterns and rhythms of Earth’s surface at different time steps.

A summary of each challenge will be released on September 17, followed by challenge statements on October 28, which include the full details and requirements. Resources for each challenge will be published on November 13. Teams **are not allowed** to begin working on the challenges prior to the hackathon.

We appreciate the enthusiasm of participants who want to start as early as possible. However, participants should NOT begin working on their project until the hackathon begins on November 14, 2026 (9:00 a.m. local time) to ensure a fair and equitable process.
